title: Paithani
summary: Paithani is a handwoven silk cloth from the town of Paithan in Maharashtra, woven in the tapestry manner: each patch of colour is made with its own small bobbin of silk instead of a thread running the full width. Peacocks, flowers and parrots appear as smooth blocks of colour with stepped edges, and gold thread outlines the borders.
howToPlay: Pick a thread colour and a pattern shape from the tray.
Touch a square on the cloth to weave that shape there; it is mirrored on the other side of the centre line.
Copy the panel shown on the card, then press Check.
rules: The panel is mirrored left and right, so every shape you place also appears on its partner square.
A square counts only when its shape and its thread colour both match the pattern you are copying.
Three stars need a nearly perfect copy; you can undo or clear as often as you like.
heritageNote: Paithani takes its name from the town of Paithan, and the peacock is its best-known motif. Because every motif is built up from separate coloured wefts, a single cloth can take many months to weave.
